contractFindings.apiContract: Function-scoped pseudocode. The product and benchmark subject call product.query.decompile(snapshot, address) once per function and store `value.pseudocode`. There is no API that returns a translation unit, so cross-function completeness (globals, prototypes, entry point) is outside the current contract.
contractFindings.declarationEmitterExists: semantic path: no; legacy path: stack slots only
contractFindings.twoTypeVocabularies: yes - bare (uint64) in type recovery, *_t in the C printer
contractFindings.consequence: Part of the raw-TU failure is a contract mismatch that a prelude cannot fix (no prototype/global/runtime declaration concept exists), and part is genuine intra-function emission defects that persist when a single function is compiled alone.

singleFunctionProbe.interpretation: 31.1% of individual function bodies are already valid C functions. The remaining 68.9% fail even in isolation, so their defects are emitter-scoped and cannot be explained by concatenation.

clusters.title: undeclared global data symbol (global_<addr>)
clusters.rootCause: Global data is rendered as an address-derived identifier (global_<addr>) synthesised at print time from the memory location. No global declaration list is ever emitted; the printed program has no place to put one.
clusters.fixClass: emit a global declaration block from the location table (new TU ownership boundary)

clusters.title: C++ mangled symbol emitted as a C identifier and never declared
clusters.rootCause: Mangled C++ symbol names are emitted verbatim as C identifiers and called with no prototype. Distinct from A-MISSING-PROTOTYPE because the identifier itself is not a valid C-symbol contract.
clusters.fixClass: demangle/escape non-C symbol names at the symbol boundary

representative.message: implicit declaration of function 'Z_tst64' is invalid in C99 [-Wimplicit-function-declaration]

clusters.title: missing external function prototype (sub_<addr> and named callees)
clusters.rootCause: Decompilation is function-scoped: the product API returns one function's pseudocode (subject.mjs calls product.query.decompile per address). Nothing within a function render can declare a callee defined elsewhere, so calls precede definitions with no prototype. This is a genuine translation-unit ownership gap, not an emitter bug.
clusters.contract: function-scoped pseudocode render; no TU ownership boundary exists
clusters.fixClass: introduce a TU assembly layer that emits prototypes (does not exist today)

representative.message: implicit declaration of function 'sub_8E0' is invalid in C99 [-Wimplicit-function-declaration]

clusters.title: undeclared user/engine type name
clusters.rootCause: User/engine type names (vector128, Base, Derived, Container, std) are used as types or in cast position with no type declaration; no struct or typedef block is emitted.
clusters.fixClass: emit nominal type declarations (aggregate recovery already exists in phase8/aggregates.js)

clusters.title: non-standard integer type alias (uint32 / uint64 / int64 / uint8)
clusters.rootCause: Two type-name vocabularies coexist. Type recovery names widths with bare non-standard aliases (uint64/uint32/int64/uint8) and semanticSignature renders those names verbatim into the declarator; the C expression printer uses the *_t spelling. Nothing emits a typedef or a <stdint.h> include.
clusters.contract: type naming vocabulary used by the signature renderer
clusters.fixClass: unify the type vocabulary and emit a prelude/typedef block

clusters.title: undeclared decompiler runtime / pseudo-intrinsic helper
clusters.rootCause: `unknown_call` is not a designed runtime helper. It is the sentinel the C printer substitutes when a call has no resolved callee, so an unresolved call target is printed as a call to a symbol that does not exist. The pseudo-intrinsics (phi, bit_extract, bit_insert, sext, __a64_movi_*,\n__arm64_condition_*, __arm64_nzcv_*) are printed as ordinary calls with no declaration. The IR does know the target is unresolved (ctx.unknownCallArities is tracked), so this is a contract leak rather than missing analysis.
clusters.fixClass: declare the runtime/intrinsic surface, or render an explicit unresolved-call form

representative.message: implicit declaration of function 'unknown_call' is invalid in C99 [-Wimplicit-function-declaration]

clusters.title: standard fixed-width alias used without <stdint.h>
clusters.rootCause: The expression printer emits uint32_t/uint64_t/int32_t casts, which are correct C names but require <stdint.h>. No include or typedef is emitted anywhere, so the same translation unit mixes `uint64 f(void)` (bare, from type recovery) with `(uint32_t)a1` (from the printer).
clusters.contract: type rendering / missing standard header emission
clusters.fixClass: emit a deterministic prelude (typedefs or <stdint.h>)

clusters.title: call argument count contradicts an emitted zero-arg declaration
clusters.rootCause: Derived from A-MISSING-PROTOTYPE: an earlier zero-arg implicit declaration contradicts a later call.
clusters.fixClass: same fix as A-MISSING-PROTOTYPE

representative.message: too many arguments to function call, expected 0, have 1

clusters.title: same emitted symbol defined more than once
clusters.rootCause: The unnamed-function placeholder name `$x` is reused for distinct functions in the same translation unit.
clusters.fixClass: make placeholder names unique per emitted symbol

clusters.title: entry point rendered with a non-int return type
clusters.rootCause: No entry-point special case: `main` is rendered with whatever return type type recovery produced (void), producing `void main(void)`.
clusters.fixClass: model the entry point contract when the TU is assembled

clusters.title: later definition conflicts with an earlier implicit declaration
clusters.rootCause: Derived from A-MISSING-PROTOTYPE: a call before the definition creates an implicit `int f()`.
clusters.fixClass: same fix as A-MISSING-PROTOTYPE

clusters.title: declaration with incomplete type
clusters.rootCause: Derived from B-INVALID-DECLARATOR-NAME: `void Container::get(...)` parses as a variable of type void.
clusters.fixClass: same fix as B-INVALID-DECLARATOR-NAME

clusters.title: invalid C declarator name (C++ qualified / demangled names)
clusters.rootCause: C++ qualified/demangled names (`thunk to MultiDerived::funcB`, `Container::get`) are emitted as C declarators, which is not valid C.
clusters.fixClass: escape non-identifier characters at the declarator boundary

clusters.title: member access on a non-struct base (dotted symbol names)
clusters.rootCause: Dotted symbol names (param_atomic_ops.constprop.0) are emitted as C identifiers, so `.` parses as member access.
clusters.fixClass: escape `.` at the symbol boundary

representative.message: member reference base type 'void (void)' is not a structure or union

clusters.title: label emitted before the function body compound statement
clusters.rootCause: ensureLegacyLabel searches for the first line with row >= target row; if that search fails it falls back to the closing-brace line, and if THAT also fails it clamps to index 1. Index 1 is between the `sig` line (index 0) and the `{` line (index 1), i.e. inside the function declarator, before the body. The clamp `Math.max(1, ...)` was meant to keep the label below the signature but index 1 is still above `{`; the correct floor is 2.
clusters.contract: label insertion anchor vs function prologue
clusters.fixClass: clamp the label insertion anchor to the first body line (index >= 2)

representative.message: expected function body after function declarator

clusters.title: malformed expression caused by an undeclared type name
clusters.rootCause: Derived from A-NONSTANDARD-INT-ALIAS: `*(uint64 *)0x13FD0` cannot parse without the type.
clusters.fixClass: same fix as A-NONSTANDARD-INT-ALIAS

clusters.title: statement emitted outside any function body
clusters.rootCause: ensureLegacyGoto anchors its insertion at the last line whose `row` is <= the source edge's end row, then splices at anchor+1. The legacy renderer stamps its closing `}` line with the last instruction row (decompile-legacy.js:139), so that anchor can BE the closing brace; the synthesised goto then lands after `}` at file scope.
clusters.contract: statement insertion anchor vs function epilogue

sourceLocations.symbol: closing brace carries a real row

clusters.fixClass: exclude the closing-brace line from the goto insertion anchor search

clusters.title: string literal combined with arithmetic instead of concatenation
clusters.rootCause: A string literal operand is combined arithmetically (`"\n" + 24`).
clusters.fixClass: model string-literal operands as pointer values

representative.message: adding 'int' to a string does not append to the string [-Wstring-plus-int]

clusters.title: undeclared raw architecture register (sp, lr, pc)
clusters.rootCause: Raw architecture registers (sp, lr, pc) are printed as C identifiers.
clusters.fixClass: declare or eliminate raw register names

clusters.title: undeclared parameter/return pseudo-variable (a1, a2, v0, ...)
clusters.rootCause: The signature renderer and the body renderer disagree about parameters. semanticSignature renders a1..aN only for recovered args, but the body still names ABI argument registers a1, a2, a3 - so `void sequential_ops(void)` has a body reading a1..a3. Either the signature must declare them or the body must not name them.
clusters.contract: function signature rendering vs body variable rendering
clusters.fixClass: emit a consistent parameter contract (declare args or bind register names)

clusters.title: undeclared generated call temporary (call_<n>)
clusters.rootCause: Per-call result temporaries are created as AST variables named call_<id> for the call's IR value id, emitted inline in statements, and never declared. The emitter knows they are temporaries ({materializedCall:true}), so the declaration is missing rather than unknowable.
clusters.contract: temporary generation inside the body emitter
clusters.fixClass: declare generated call temporaries in the body prologue

clusters.title: undeclared condition temporary (condition_*)
clusters.rootCause: Condition/flag temporaries (condition_eq, condition_le, flag_eq) are referenced in branch conditions without declaration.
clusters.fixClass: declare condition temporaries in the body prologue

clusters.title: goto to a label the emitted body never defines
clusters.rootCause: Control-flow structuring emits `goto loc_<hex>` for edges whose target block is not emitted with a matching label (104/160 cases, 251 distinct labels). The structuring and the label emission disagree about which blocks are materialised.
clusters.fixClass: make label emission and goto emission share one block-materialisation set (fail closed)

clusters.title: undeclared SSA phi temporary (local_phi_*)
clusters.rootCause: SSA phi results are emitted as identifiers `local_phi_<id>` ({phi:true}), never declared, and never lowered into locals. A second, independent phi encoding exits as `phi(a, b)` calls (A-RUNTIME-HELPER-DECL), so phi handling is not even internally consistent.
clusters.fixClass: lower phi temporaries into declared locals, or declare them

clusters.title: undeclared register pseudo-variable (x0, x19, w0, d0, ...)
clusters.rootCause: Register/high-variable names (x0, x0_1, x19, w0, d0) escape into the body as ordinary identifiers with no declaration. Same missing decl path as B-UNDECLARED-STACK-SLOT, but these are not part of types.locals, so even the legacy decl emitter would not cover them.

sourceLocations.symbol: no decl emitter in the semantic path

clusters.fixClass: declare every materialised pseudo-variable in the body prologue

clusters.title: undeclared stack-slot / local-memory pseudo-variable
clusters.rootCause: The semantic renderer emits no declaration lines at all. decompileSemantic assembles lines as [sig, '{', ...body, '}'] and the line-kind vocabulary (sig/ctrl/stmt/label) contains no 'decl' kind, so stack-slot names (local_<off>, local_p<hex>, var_<off>) that the body writes are never declared. The legacy renderer does have a declaration block, but the semantic path - the IR-first default - does not.
clusters.fixClass: emit a declaration block from the recovered locals (the legacy path already models it)

clusters.title: undeclared value/return pseudo-variable (v0, v165, v1010, ...)
clusters.rootCause: SSA value indices are printed with a `v` prefix (v165, v1010) and used as operands with no declaration. Shares the spelling space with ARM64 SIMD registers v0..v31, which the same renderer also prints.
clusters.fixClass: declare materialised SSA values (or inline them into their single use)

clusters.title: unresolved operand emitted as a literal `?` token
clusters.rootCause: A literal `?` token is emitted in operand position on both sides of an assignment (`? = *(uint64 *)(x1);`). A printer placeholder escapes as a token instead of a value; the emitter has an unresolved operand and prints `?`.
clusters.fixClass: render an explicit unresolved-operand form instead of a bare `?`

clusters.title: parser recovery diagnostic caused by an earlier undeclared type
clusters.rootCause: Parser recovery after an undeclared alias; not an independent defect.
clusters.fixClass: disappears with the type-alias fix

clusters.title: compiler note attached to a parent diagnostic
clusters.rootCause: clang notes attached to a parent error; evidence, not defects.
clusters.fixClass: none

clusters.title: unclassified diagnostic
clusters.rootCause: No diagnostic left unclassified after the alias-declaration cascade rule.
clusters.fixClass: none

clusters.title: environment / toolchain only
clusters.rootCause: Host toolchain only; no environment-caused failure was observed.
clusters.fixClass: none
